exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Row Operation Equivalent To Left Multiplication by an Elementary Matrix

question.text: Consider $E = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ Find the row operation that, when applied to $A,$ is equivalent to multiplying $A$ by the given elementary matrix $E$ from the left.
question.explanation:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by taking the first row of $I_3$ and adding $2$ times the third row:

\begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 &:= R_1 + 2R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E \end{align*}

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation $R_1 := R_1 + 2R_3$ to $A.$

question.explanation:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by taking the third row of $I_3$ and adding $7$ times the first row:

\begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_3 &:= R_3+7R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 7 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E \end{align*}

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation $R_3:=R_3+7R_1$ to $A.$

question.text: Consider $E = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ Find the row operation that, when applied to $A,$ is equivalent to multiplying $A$ by the given elementary matrix $E$ from the left.
question.explanation:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by swapping the first and the second rows of $I_3\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} I_3 &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 &\leftrightarrow R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E \end{align*}

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2$ to $A.$

question.text: Suppose that the elementary row operation $R_1 := \dfrac{5}{2}R_1$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
question.explanation:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation $R_1 := \dfrac{5}{2}R_1$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

\begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 & := \dfrac{5}{2}R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{5}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E \end{align*}

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{5}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

question.text: Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order: \[ R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2, \qquad R_3 :=R_3-4R_1, \qquad R_1 := -8R_1 \] What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
question.explanation:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 &\leftrightarrow R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_1 \end{align*}

  • The second operation is $R_3 :=R_3-4R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_3 & :=R_3-4R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_2 \end{align*}

  • The third operation is $R_1 := -8R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 & := -8R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} -8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_3 \end{align*}

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by $E_1$ on the left and get $E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 0& 1 & 0 \\ 1& 0 & 0 \\ 0& 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to $E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_2$ on the left and get $E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0& 1 & 0 \\ 1& 0 & 0 \\ 0& 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to $E_2E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_3$ on the left and get $E_3E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} -8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0& 1 & 0 \\ 1& 0 & 0 \\ 0& 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_3.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 &\leftrightarrow R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_1 \end{align*}

  • The second operation is $R_2 :=R_2-2R_3.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 & :=R_2-2R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_2 \end{align*}

  • The third operation is $R_1 := 3R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 & := 3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_3 \end{align*}

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by $E_1$ on the left and get $E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to $E_2E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_3$ on the left and get $E_3E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0& 0 & 1 \\ 0& 1 & 0 \\ 1& 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]
